explanations: Gold is element 79, symbol Au, one of the least reactive elements, and about half the new supply each year becomes jewellery.
Silver is a soft, lustrous metal with the highest electrical and thermal conductivity of any metal, and its halides made photography possible.
Bronze is an alloy of copper with about 12 per cent tin, and gave its name to the age before the Iron Age.
Gold, silver and bronze are the three classes of Olympic medal, awarded for first, second and third place.

sources.excerpt: Gold is a chemical element; its chemical symbol is Au (from Latin aurum) and atomic number 79.
It is one of the least reactive chemical elements, being the second lowest in the reactivity series, with only platinum ranked as less reactive.
The world's consumption of new gold produced is about 50% in jewelry, 40% in investments, and 10% in industry.
A soft, white, lustrous transition metal, it exhibits the highest electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity and reflectivity of any metal.
Silver halides are important in photographic film, photographic paper and photochromic glass, although demand for photographic silver has declined with the spread of digital imaging.

Bronze is an alloy consisting primarily of copper, commonly with about 12–12.5% tin and often with the addition of other metals (including aluminium, manganese, nickel, or zinc) and sometimes non-metals (such as phosphorus) or metalloids (such as arsenic or silicon).
The archaeological period during which bronze was the hardest metal in widespread use is known as the Bronze Age.

An Olympic medal is an honorary medal that is awarded to successful competitors at one of the Olympic Games. There are three classes of medal to be won: gold, silver, and bronze, awarded to first, second, and third place, respectively.

editorNotes: Alternatives checked: the three are also the standard placings in many other competitions, but only the Olympic protocols lay out three classes of medal in this way; 'the Bronze Age' is named in a clue as a period, not as the answer; brass is copper with zinc, not tin.
